title: CNI route flap causing AZ-isolated service blackhole — triage notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working triage log for the incident on 2026-02-24 where a subset of nodes in us-west-2a experienced a CNI route table flap that caused Service IPs to become effectively blackholed from other AZs and some pods in the same AZ. Symptoms: intermittent 5xxs from internal services, increased request latency, sporadic DNS timeouts, and sudden pod-to-pod TCP reset spikes for traffic traversing node-local egress paths.

Why this doc exists: collect quick investigation notes, short-term mitigations applied, hypotheses for root cause, and recommended runbook additions / long-term fixes. This is intentionally informal; preserve raw commands and outputs for later postmortem.

Incident timeline (local times):
- 2026-02-24 03:12 UTC — monitoring alert: internal API p95 latency > 2s and error rate spike in service-owner-metadata.
- 2026-02-24 03:14 UTC — SRE oncall (Maya) starts live triage; pagerduty escalations initiated.
- 2026-02-24 03:16 UTC — Additional alerts: cross-AZ kube-proxy conntrack errors and kube-system Cilium pods showing high restart counts in us-west-2a.
- 2026-02-24 03:20 UTC — Confirmed affected node set: nodepool-gpu-usw2a-[a-c] (3 nodes). Other AZs nominal.
- 2026-02-24 03:22 UTC — Observed: Service IPs for redis-internal and metrics-scraper returned syn-ack/fin resets from some client nodes; tcpdump shows SYN to ServiceIP arriving on node but no backend response.
- 2026-02-24 03:28 UTC — Attempted quick mitigation: restart cilium-agent on node-a (kubectl delete pod -n kube-system cilium-xxxx on node-a). Partial recovery for node-a; node-b and node-c still flapping.
- 2026-02-24 03:45 UTC — Scaled nodepool up by +2 nodes in us-west-2a to give scheduler capacity and to move some traffic off suspected bad nodes.
- 2026-02-24 04:12 UTC — Network team confirmed cloud VPC route table propagation events around 03:08-03:18 UTC during a transient API call to ASG autoscaler (scale-down succeeded earlier and a new scaledown triggered).
- 2026-02-24 04:50 UTC — Implemented rolling cordon+drain and full cilium restart across the 3 affected nodes; services stabilized by ~05:05 UTC.

Immediate observations / reproducible checks performed:
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep cilium showed restarts only in the three affected nodes.
- journalctl -u cilium-agent on affected nodes showed repeated errors: "program route entry delete failed: file exists" and "failed to program NodePort: conflicting host routes".
- ip route show on affected nodes intermittently missing expected service routes for ClusterIP ranges (10.96.0.0/12) when failures observed.
- cilium bpf monitor revealed brief spikes of rejected map updates and errno=22 on route replace syscalls on nodes during the window.
- cloud VPC routes: console showed rapid create/delete for ENI prefix routes coincident with autoscaler events.
- conntrack dumps on control nodes had large number of short-lived entries for Service IPs with TTL < 5s.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Reconciliation race between Cilium eBPF route programming and cloud route table updates during node scale events. When an ENI route is removed and re-added, the Cilium agent's local route reconciliation attempts can hit kernel EFAULTs (or EINVAL) causing partial route table state and temporary blackholes.
2) A cilium version bug in our current branch that mishandles replace/delete of host-scoped routes under heavy churn (seen as "file exists" / errno=22 in logs). This is consistent with a recent operator upgrade last month.
3) Underlying kernel bug/driver (Nitro ENI plugin) on that instance type + AZ causing transient route table inconsistencies only visible when route churn occurs.

Short-term mitigations applied (effectiveness notes):
- Restarted cilium-agent on affected nodes — immediate partial recovery on first restart; subsequent restarts needed for others. Effectiveness: medium.
- Cordon + drain: moved workloads away from affected nodes; removed pressure on host routes. Effectiveness: high for customer impact (but disruptive).
- Temporarily disabled aggressive node-scale-down in the autoscaler config for the pool (scale-down-disabled: 15m). Effectiveness: prevented recurrence during incident window.
- Increased liveness probe timeout for cilium-agent to reduce operator churn while kernel reconciles. Effectiveness: low-to-medium; avoided cascading restarts.

Data to collect next time (instrumentation additions):
- Export cilium_agent_program_errors metric (errno tags) to alert on > 5/min per node.
- Add eBPF map saturation and rejects as a cloudwatch/grafana panel.
- Track VPC route create/delete rate per AZ and correlate with k8s node events.
- Conntrack churn metric per service IP with p99 TTL.

Immediate post-incident action items (owners assigned):
- eng-sre (Maya) — add alert: cilium.route_program_failures > 1/min (2026-03-02 complete).
- infra-networking (Priya) — investigate cloud ENI driver kernel logs on instance type i3en.large in us-west-2a; ask cloud provider support if repeated. (ticket opened: SRE-2182).
- platform (Noah) — pin problematic nodepool autoscaler setting to avoid aggressive scale-downs until we patch (done temporary).
- eng-sre (Ethan) — reproduce offline in staging with forced route churn using cilium-chaos tooling and capture bpf logs. (job scheduled).

Runbook additions (draft):
- Detection checklist: if Service 5xx spike + errors in cilium logs with "route" or "replace":
  - Run: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady / kube-system restarts
  - Run: ssh to node -> sudo ip route show; sudo cilium status --wait; sudo journalctl -u cilium-agent --since "15m" | grep -i error
  - Run: cilium bpf list-maps && cilium bpf map get <map> for map fill %
  - If route entries missing, cordon+drain the node and restart cilium-agent.
- Fast remediation steps:
  1) Identify all nodes in the same AZ with cilium-agent restarts (kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide).
  2) For each affected node: run "sudo ip route show" and save output to incident bucket.
  3) Restart cilium-agent and watch cilium status; if fails twice, cordon+drain and rotate the node.
  4) If multiple nodes affected, temporarily disable scale-down on pool and notify network team.
- Forensic checklist: collect cilium-agent logs, bpf monitor output, conntrack dumps, cloud route activity logs, and node syslogs.

Longer-term mitigations and engineering roadmap items:
- Backport/upgrade cilium to a release with the route-replace robustness fixes (PR linked above). Target: 1.11.x -> coordinator has approval to schedule in next maintenance window.
- Add explicit recovery reconciliation: if host route programming fails, cilium operator should wait and retry with exponential backoff instead of proceeding. (Assign: eng-serving-runtime / cilium-operator owners).
- Improve autoscaler safety: do not allow scale-down that removes >1 node from a given AZ within 10 minutes. (Platform ticket).
- Add a gating e2e test in CI that simulates ENI/route churn and ensures Cilium keeps service connectivity.

Notes / open questions:
- Why did only us-west-2a nodes exhibit the issue? Early theory: subtle kernel module version skew on instances in that AZ from a recent AMI bake. Need to collect /boot/config-$(uname -r) and modinfo outputs.
- Was there any upstream cloud event causing route churn? Network team to pull cloud control plane logs.
- Are there related low-severity incidents in the last 30 days that suggest slow buildup? Search for "route_program" errors historically.

Raw commands used during triage (copy-paste friendly):
- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep cilium
- kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "NotReady|SchedulingDisabled"
- ssh ec2-user@node-a sudo ip route show > /tmp/node-a-routes.txt
- ssh ec2-user@node-a sudo journalctl -u cilium-agent --no-pager --since "2026-02-24 02:00" | grep -i "route\|replace\|errno\|error" > /tmp/cilium-errors.txt
- sudo cilium bpf monitor --type program
- sudo conntrack -L | grep 10.96.0.0/12 | wc -l

Postmortem draft outline (to be expanded):
1) Summary / impact (customer-facing blurb)
2) Timeline (cleaned)
3) Root cause analysis (race between cloud route churn and Cilium eBPF programming + operator bug)
4) Contributing factors (autoscaler aggressiveness, missing route-program metrics, possible AMI kernel skew)
5) Remediation (what we did)
6) Long-term fixes (upgrade, autoscaler safety, CI chaos test)
7) Action items with owners and completion dates

Appendix: snippets of key logs (sanitized)
- "level=error msg="program route replace failed: errno=22""
- "host routes mismatch: expected 10.96.0.0/12 -> dev cilium_host: route absent"

If you worked on any of the quick fixes, add notes below with timestamps so we can build the cleaned timeline for the postmortem.

-- maya
